correctness.rationale: An exact conditioned composition formula yields a fixed-count partition-sector limit \(b^{k-1}/[k!(k-1)!]\) under \(\theta_L/L^2\to\Theta\). A factorially summable uniform bound permits summing all counts, and bounded-support Hoeffding bounds eliminate the zero-cluster sector. Under fixed-count conditioning, polynomial bulk reweighting preserves concentration at \(\mu\), and uniform weak compositions yield \(\operatorname{Dirichlet}(1,\ldots,1)\) mass proportions scaled by \(e\). The analytic argument proves the joint limit; checker.py agrees independently with all directly enumerated small cases and converges numerically to the Bessel law. No numerical extrapolation is used to justify the theorem.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2024 primary article explicitly leaves the \(\gamma=2\) law unresolved, including the finite macroscopic cluster count and coupled masses. A 2026 generalization also excludes its critical line; its \(\kappa=0\) constant-tail case falls exactly here. The inclusion-process Poisson–Dirichlet result is not equivalent. Focused source, claim, alias and parameter searches and comparisons found no covering published statement; there remains a substantive but nondecisive risk of unindexed duplicate results.
residual_risks: The existing 2024 cluster partition-function decomposition almost contains the computation; an unindexed informal or follow-up derivation might already evaluate the critical limit.
A stronger general theorem beyond the inspected 2026 article could conceivably imply the same Bessel–Dirichlet law; no such coverage was found.

value.rationale: The critical exponent \(\gamma=2\) is the physically singled-out boundary between diverging mesoscopic and uniquely macroscopic condensates. The exact count probability and complete random mass split resolve a published natural structural question and distinguish finite-simplex partitions from the known Poisson–Dirichlet and independent-cluster regimes. The result is a nontrivial universal stationary law with a direct probability-of-one-condensate interpretation; it makes no unsupported dynamical claim.
